scenes.title: Checkout froze. Did payment succeed?
scenes.label: ASHA'S CHECKOUT
scenes.voice: Asha taps Place Order. Checkout stalls. She cannot tell whether payment succeeded. A slow request alone does not prove garbage collection caused it.
scenes.note: Customer symptom first. Diagnose the cause before changing flags.

scenes.title: The heap is Java's workbench
scenes.label: WHAT GARBAGE COLLECTION DOES
scenes.voice: The Java heap holds objects. Garbage collection reclaims unreachable objects. Some phases pause application threads; other phases run alongside them.
scenes.note: Reachable objects stay. Unreachable objects can be reclaimed.

scenes.title: 2,000 ms request. 300 ms pause.
scenes.label: FOLLOW THE TIMELINE
scenes.voice: This example request takes two seconds. An overlapping pause lasts three hundred milliseconds. The bank also takes time. Do not blame the entire delay on garbage collection.
scenes.note: Constructed evidence on one server; no benchmark claim.

scenes.title: An overlap is a clue, not a verdict
scenes.label: COMPARE THE EVIDENCE
scenes.voice: Match request traces and pause logs from the same server. Check payment waits, database spans, and CPU before deciding what to fix.
scenes.note: Intervals can overlap. Do not add the same time twice.

scenes.title: Fix proven redundant work
scenes.label: PROFILE, CHANGE, REPEAT
scenes.voice: Use Java Flight Recorder to find allocation hotspots. Remove redundant work without changing order totals. Compare the same workload before choosing another collector.
scenes.note: Fewer unnecessary objects; unchanged business calculations.

scenes.title: Responsive checkout. Correct payment.
scenes.label: VALIDATE AND RECOVER
scenes.voice: Validate tail latency, errors, memory, and CPU. Keep the original payment identity and reconcile uncertain outcomes. A timeout is not proof of failed payment.
scenes.note: Confirm only after an authoritative payment result.
